1.explanation: We reproduce the bug by shelling out to the Lighthouse CLI exactly as the user did in their screenshot. By passing an invalid URL (or one that Chrome can’t load), you force the CLI into its fatal error branch. In that branch the code currently prints the ICU template identifier rather than looking up the localized string. The script above captures both stdout and stderr so you can see the raw template key in stderr, confirming the missing translation step.
1.bug_scenario:
When you invoke the Lighthouse CLI with a URL that ultimately causes a fatal runtime error (for example by using an invalid URL or causing Chrome to fail to load the page), the CLI prints the raw ICU template identifier (“lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0”) instead of the localized, human-friendly error message. The screenshot shows exactly that: a Chrome launch sequence followed by

  Runtime error encountered: lighthouse-core/lib/lh-error.js | urlInvalid # 0
  LHEError: INVALID_URL
  at lighthouse …

indicating that the i18n lookup never happened on the fatal error path.
